You can't tell which version is worth building, so none of them gets built, and the whole thing waits.

You don't need a clearer sign. You need one small piece of the work to leave your hands and land somewhere real. That's how direction comes back — not from resolving the whole picture, but from letting one rough thing be seen and hearing what it makes in someone else. What you want hasn't gone anywhere. It's just been waiting for the next move to be smaller than it looks.
3.sheetLine: One unfinished thing, shown to someone, finds more than thinking does.

4.tense: You are already shaping what is coming together, and you talk about it as if it were assembling itself.
4.verb: imagining something until it feels fully real
4.place: somewhere between not enough light to see and enough to take the next step
4.ask: Name one choice you made this week that actually went the way you wanted, and say out loud that you did that. Not the timing, not the luck. You.
4.core:
The work is happening — imagining things into shape, feeling them through, letting satisfaction land where it's earned. But you'd probably describe it as just happening. The ideas arrived, the pieces fit, it worked out. You don't take the pen for any of it.

That's what makes this hard to see: when it's running well, the dreaming and the doing feel like one motion, clean enough that you can't tell where you ended and the flow began. But you did bring it together — your attention, your patience, your willingness to feel it through to the end. Calling that yours isn't arrogance. It's just accuracy.
4.sheetLine: You did bring this together. Say so out loud.

1.tense: What was imagined is being felt as real, and the feeling is landing in your body.
1.verb: letting what was imagined be felt as enough, with your own feelings as the copy
1.place: the workshop where you stop copying others' finished shapes and build from your own grain
1.ask: Once this week, make something small and keep it private. When it's done, sit with it a few minutes and let one honest reaction — satisfaction or restlessness — be felt fully without fixing it.
1.core:
You can feel when a thing is finished, and you trust the feeling. What you picture, you can make, and the satisfaction of having made it lands in your body as real. That loop runs clean: you feel your way toward what wants to be made, you make it, you let the making land.

Now watch where that loop is free to go next. Because you can feel completion, you can be generous with it — hand over the part of your vision no one has asked for yet, or let someone watch you work before it is pretty. The only thing that would starve this is treating the satisfaction as something you keep for yourself because no one else would get it. The doors are already open. Walk through one.
1.sheetLine: You can feel what is finished, and you trust the feeling.

2.tense: You're already building the thing that will finally prove the vision true.
2.verb: letting what was imagined be felt as enough, with your own feelings as the copy
2.place: the workshop where you stop copying others' finished shapes and build from your own grain
2.ask: Take one piece of the vision and set it on a surface where others can touch it — a sketch, a prototype, half of the math — before you have the next step figured out. Put it there and leave it.
2.core:
The making is still happening, but you've started working for the imagined ending rather than from what you can feel today. You can hear yourself saying it's not there yet, so you push harder, reach further, and refuse to call anything finished. The completion you used to trust has been replaced by a future that keeps moving.

What you are straining toward is a moment when someone looks at what you made and gets it, and you are trying to arrive there by force. That is exhausting, and it makes the real thing you already have — the ability to imagine and then feel it as real — look like something still to be earned. The care is genuine. The clutch is not. You get further by holding the work loosely, letting other hands steady it, and letting the finish come when it comes.
2.sheetLine: You're gripping the ending so hard the work can't arrive.

3.tense: You were standing at the door when the thing you imagined was ready to be seen.
3.verb: letting what was imagined be felt as enough, with your own feelings as the copy
3.place: the workshop where you stop copying others' finished shapes and build from your own grain
3.ask: Pick the smallest piece of what you imagined — one page, one small build, one short recording of your own voice — and finish it today. No one has to see it yet. Just make it exist outside your head.
3.core:
The imagining still runs. You can still feel what would be satisfying if you let yourself. But at some point, showing it or finishing it started to ask more than you had, so you pulled back and kept it private. The door is behind you now, and you are still describing yourself as someone who is about to, or might, or used to.

There is no shortage of vision here. What has gone quiet is the move from inside to out. Start with the smallest finished thing you can stand to make, and let the quiet knowing that knows when it is done come back online. It will feel like weight lifting off, not like effort being poured in.
3.sheetLine: You stopped at the door, and the unfinished thing is still there.

4.tense: The copy of the vision is already being made, but you haven't put your name on it.
4.verb: letting what was imagined be felt as enough, with your own feelings as the copy
4.place: the workshop where you stop copying others' finished shapes and build from your own grain
4.ask: Find one piece of work you've been calling just practice, name what it's actually reaching for, out loud, to no one in particular. Then keep going.
4.core:
The thing is being made — through your body, your habits, the way you show up — and you describe it as practice, or admin, or just the way things are. The steering is running in the background, and you have not claimed it. What you call discipline is imagination staying private and modest on purpose.

Your actual work right now is smaller than you think, but not less real: it is you letting yourself admit that the practice and the making are the same activity, and that you are already in it. The refinement will keep going. Finish here, not somewhere else. The point is not to make the practice more serious. The point is to stop describing your own hand as the room's.
4.sheetLine: The work is yours. You've been calling it something else.

1.tense: You are standing at the far side of an imagining that has become real enough to feel.
1.verb: Imagining a life of your own and feeling it through until the first full yes, the one experience cannot take back.
1.place: Standing far enough back to see the whole pattern, still inside it.
1.ask: Take the one you have been circling and make it concrete for someone today: put it where they can see it, in a form they can hold.
1.core: Something you imagined long enough and felt deeply enough has arrived at the far side of the imagining, and the satisfaction is real. You can see the whole pattern of it — how the pieces came, what they add up to now. That is a good place to stand, holding a larger picture in view while staying inside it. It isn't perfect, and it doesn't have to be. Being satisfied with what was imagined feels unusual, like standing somewhere you aren't supposed to stay. You are free to keep what arrived, to choose the imagined life and live inside it rather than walk away from it. What comes next doesn't have to be a demand; it can be something quiet, done because it fits and feels true.
1.sheetLine: What was imagined has arrived, and you can feel it.

2.tense: You are bracing in front of a life that still has to be made proof, so the imagining is running ahead of what has actually happened.
2.verb: Imagining a life of your own and feeling it through until the first full yes, the one experience cannot take back.
2.place: Standing far enough back to see the whole pattern, still inside it.
2.ask: Pick one seed and tend it this week — the same one — and let that be the whole of the striving, nothing extra.
2.core: You keep trying to hold the whole pattern steady, and your grip is going past what one hand can carry. Every version of the future gets sorted, compared, held up against the next version before any of it has had time to grow. The largeness you are waiting for hasn't arrived, and you are treating that as a problem you can force into shape. Some of what you want is already in front of you in a smaller form; it is being passed over. Care that clutches takes energy and gives panic back. The way through isn't a bigger plan. It is one plant you actually water. Keep it small enough to hold, and let the rest wait.
2.sheetLine: The life you want cannot be built by forcing the timing.

3.tense: You are still facing a door you once imagined opening, standing in front of it even though it closed behind you.
3.verb: Imagining a life of your own and feeling it through until the first full yes, the one experience cannot take back.
3.place: Standing far enough back to see the whole pattern, still inside it.
3.ask: Write down one word that feels true today, without judging it, and read it again tonight.
3.core: The imagining is still going on somewhere, but it stopped coming through to the present. You can see pieces of what might be true, the shape of it, and nothing lands anywhere or chooses. So nothing has arrived, and the whole picture stays out of reach. There isn't much fuel for this right now, and pushing harder only makes the quiet louder. What charges it is smaller. One honest word, kept to yourself for a while, proves more than a large conclusion forced out too soon. Trusting you can be sure of things without announcing them keeps the imagining from becoming a promise you rush to keep. Pick one thing to know quietly.
3.sheetLine: It is safe to know what you know before you say it.

4.tense: You are already making the life you imagined, and you tell the story as if it arrived on its own.
4.verb: Imagining a life of your own and feeling it through until the first full yes, the one experience cannot take back.
4.place: Standing far enough back to see the whole pattern, still inside it.
4.ask: Name one thing you made that you call luck or timing, and say you did it. Do it once, out loud.
4.core: The imagining has been going on the whole time — and it has been yours. The choices that grew into this were made by you, one at a time, and the whole pattern only holds together because you kept working it. What gets said is that things just happened, or the moment was right, or someone else set it up. The making is still going; it hasn't stopped. The credit is sitting right next to the work, waiting. Once you take one piece of it in your own hand, the whole picture sharpens, because it finally has an author. You can see the pattern without needing it to have been given to you.
4.sheetLine: The life you wanted is one you made.

1.tense: One imagined thing has been fully felt, and it has added up.
1.verb: Letting what you imagined be fully felt, and letting that add up
1.place: The threshold where you finish something and let it go, so the next thing can start
1.ask: Show the finished thing to one person this week, without touching it up first.
1.core:
One piece of what you imagined has been carried all the way — seen, felt, and worth keeping as it is. Not because everything came out perfect, but because it got all the way through you and out the other side. That kind of satisfaction can't be planned for. It only shows up after the fact.

The power here is knowing when to stop. What you made is finished; it can be let go. You're standing where finishing gives the next thing its start. The worth of what you made isn't sitting in a total you could count. Your next move is small, and it keeps the door open instead of closing it.
1.sheetLine: One thing you made has been felt all the way through.

2.tense: Your satisfaction is still ahead of you, in a scene not yet written.
2.verb: Letting what you imagined be fully felt, and letting that add up
2.place: The threshold where you finish something and let it go, so the next thing can start
2.ask: Pick one thing you've made and leave it alone for a week, finished or not.
2.core:
You're living ahead of your own work, rehearsing the satisfaction before the thing is finished. What you imagined gets felt, but it gets felt too fast — before it has run through you — and so it stays slightly out of reach, and you keep reaching for the next. You're holding onto a past version of what you wanted and calling it an outcome.

The vision came from somewhere real. It earned its shape. But it can't grow if you keep pulling on it to check that it's growing. Give one piece of it a week where nobody touches it. Not checked, not improved, not steered. It's done enough to stand for seven days by itself.
2.sheetLine: You're ahead of the work, feeling the result before it's finished.

3.tense: At some point an imagined thing kept sitting there, already finished, not felt all the way.
3.verb: Letting what you imagined be fully felt, and letting that add up
3.place: The threshold where you finish something and let it go, so the next thing can start
3.ask: Take one finished thing and look at it until you can say exactly what it is.
3.core:
You left a piece of work standing at the door. It was done, or done enough, and nobody stepped through — least of all you — and the ending may not have been said out loud. So it sits there, neither kept nor let go, and you go quiet about the whole idea of having made it.

There's no more effort to push into this. The part that's thin is knowing, not feeling. Take one thing that got finished and look at it long enough to name just what it is — not what it should have been. No argument needed. If nothing comes, say that. The door doesn't need opening today; it needs seeing first.
3.sheetLine: Something got made and you stayed on this side of the door.

4.tense: All that satisfaction is already running, but you keep calling it the day's work.
4.verb: Letting what you imagined be fully felt, and letting that add up
4.place: The threshold where you finish something and let it go, so the next thing can start
4.ask: Say out loud, once, one thing you imagined that became real and is yours.
4.core:
Satisfaction is running in you right now. You feel a piece of what you made when it lands well, or when someone keeps it. It quietly steers how you do the next one. But if someone asked, you'd say the work just went well. Something is carrying weight here that nobody has signed for.

What you made didn't just happen. You imagined it, felt your way through it, and it's here. Two or three of these things are yours in a way that deserves the plain word owed. Say one of them out loud, to no one or anyone. That's the whole of it.
4.sheetLine: You feel it working. You call it the day going fine.
